extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and other stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of patent claims for subject matter eligibility under 35 U.S.C. 101 using USPTO training guidance (Steps 1, 2A, 2B), examples, and domain-specific considerations. Includes procedures for formulating rejections, evaluating applicant responses, and applying examples for abstract ideas, nature-based products, and life sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1: Statutory requirements and four categories of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Statutory requirements and four categories of invention (posted September 24, 2015).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the claimed subject matter satisfies statutory requirements and falls into one of the four statutory categories (process, machine, manufacture, composition of matter). This is the initial statutory-category inquiry before applying judicial-exception analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steps 2A and 2B: Guidance overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance overview and steps 2A and 2B (computer based training & slides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 2A: determine whether the claim is directed to a judicial exception (e.g., abstract idea, law of nature, natural phenomenon). Step 2B: if a judicial exception is present, evaluate whether the additional claim elements amount to significantly more than the judicial exception (e.g., provide inventive concept). Use the two-step framework in the USPTO guidance to structure eligibility analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2A: Revised examination procedures (2019 PEG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2A: Revised examination procedures in view of the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the 2019 PEG procedures for identifying whether claims recite judicial exceptions and how to characterize those exceptions. The training focuses on how examiners should perform Step 2A under the revised procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate Well-Understood, Routine, Conventional Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject Matter Eligibility: Well-Understood, Routine, Conventional Activity (posted May 7, 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether additional claim elements reflect activity that is well-understood, routine, and conventional to a skilled artisan at the time of the invention. If so, those elements may not supply the required 'significantly more' to render the claim patent eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract idea identification and analysis (example-based workshops)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploring Subject Matter Eligibility: Abstract Ideas (posted February 2018) and Abstract Idea Workshop I & II materials (various dates) with examples 1–8, 21, 23, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete abstract-idea examples and workshop materials to practice identifying abstract ideas and applying Steps 2A/2B. Training includes slides, handouts, blank worksheets, and answer keys to illustrate correct analyses and common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulating a subject matter eligibility rejection and evaluating the applicant’s response
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulating a subject matter eligibility rejection and evaluating the applicant’s response (June 2016), also known as Abstract Idea Workshop III.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on drafting office actions that set forth subject matter eligibility rejections and on evaluating applicant arguments and amendments in response. Includes hypothetical office actions, applicant responsive remarks, worksheets, and answer keys to train consistent, well-reasoned rejections and responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of analysis worksheets and answer keys for hypothetical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Hypothetical application, exemplary office action and applicant responsive remarks, and worksheets; worksheet answer keys; analysis worksheets for hypothetical claims 1 and 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt structured worksheets to record Step 1/2A/2B analyses for specific claims. The training provides blank worksheets and answer keys to standardize reasoning and ensure all relevant factors are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Eligibility Guidance considerations (incorporated into the MPEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim Eligibility Guidance significantly more considerations (quick reference sheet used in training) - note that this information is now incorporated into the MPEP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the broader considerations from the Interim Eligibility Guidance when analyzing eligibility; these considerations are now part of the MPEP and should inform examiner determinations and documentation of the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to retrieve case law
rubrics_metrics.description: How to retrieve case law (quick reference sheet used in training).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper retrieval and citation of relevant case law to support Step 2A/2B analyses. Examiners should locate and apply controlling and persuasive judicial decisions when identifying judicial exceptions and determining whether additional elements supply 'significantly more.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-specific evaluation: nature-based products
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzing nature-based products materials, for use with nature-based product examples 9–18 (computer based training, slides, blank worksheet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply subject-matter-eligibility principles in the context of nature-based products, using tailored examples and worksheets that address how natural products and natural phenomena are treated under the judicial-exception framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domain-specific evaluation: life sciences (life-sciences workshops)
rubrics_metrics.description: Life Sciences Workshop I materials (June 2016), for use with life sciences examples 28–33 (slides, handout, blank worksheet, worksheet answer keys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use life-sciences-specific examples and training to evaluate claims in biotech/medical fields, focusing on issues unique to laws of nature, natural phenomena, and diagnostic or therapeutic method claims under the eligibility framework.
